API-1.statement: Headless core. Check: the core starts with no screen; the runner keeps running and `orch` commands fall back to the files when the core dies.

API-10.statement: Files stay canonical. Check: deleting the core's cache and restarting gives identical answers; records survive a restart.

API-11.statement: Ordered events. Check: events have a gap-free increasing seq and the envelope {seq, ts, kind, data, v}.

API-12.statement: Resume. Check: `events.subscribe from_seq` replays exactly the missed events; an expired cursor returns cursor_expired with a snapshot.

API-13.statement: Filtering and bounds. Check: a kind filter works; a slow subscriber is dropped without delaying others or the writer.

API-14.statement: Events carry no secrets. Check: events hold ids and summaries only; a planted secret and transcript text never appear.

API-15.statement: Records-first answers. Check: canned questions (status, usage, CI, versions, history, why stopped) are answered from records with sources, as_of and tokens_used 0, and nothing is written to the inbox.

API-16.statement: Forwarding at safe points. Check: a judgment question is queued only in the inbox, delivered at a safe point as at most 300 tokens with a TTL; query.reply produces query.answered for the asker.

API-17.statement: Talk is labelled and capped. Check: context.push is labelled by source, capped (2 KB, 10 per minute), delivered as quoted untrusted data, and never counted as an owner decision.

API-18.statement: Tokens. Check: 256-bit, stored hashed, revocable, minted only at the owner's terminal (refused over the API); an agent token defaults to read plus context.push.

API-19.statement: Scope matrix. Check: read, confirm and owner scopes each allow exactly their methods; others return forbidden.

API-2.statement: Socket. Check: socket mode 0600 in a 0700 directory, path under 104 bytes, a stale socket is replaced, no TCP listener.

API-20.statement: Decisions. Check: decision.answer works for the owner role only.

API-21.statement: Two-step confirm. Check: a control call first returns confirm_required with an id; the second call within 60 s executes once; reuse, expiry and a different token or params are refused.

API-22.statement: Owner-only wall. Check: install, update, setup, reviewed install, live-record writes, billing attestation, client-range widening and token minting are refused over the API even with an owner token.

API-23.statement: Audit. Check: every change and confirm is a commands.jsonl line; every refusal is an audit.jsonl line (rotated separately, so refusals cannot push changes out); each line has caller, method, outcome; no token or secret appears.

API-24.statement: Limits. Check: request size, string length, method time, connection count and subscription count are capped with fixed error codes.

API-25.statement: Provider neutrality. Check: no provider name in method, event or field names; provider detail only under `extra`.

API-26.statement: (later adapter) HTTP+SSE bridge on 127.0.0.1 with Host/Origin/token checks, SSE id = seq. Tested with the dashboard milestone.

API-27.statement: (later adapter) stdio MCP adapter on a pinned spec exposing the same operations. Tested last.

API-3.statement: Peer identity. Check: a connection from another uid is refused before any method runs.

API-4.statement: Framing. Check: JSON-RPC 2.0 as newline-delimited JSON; a malformed line gets a parse error and the connection lives; an oversize line is refused.

API-5.statement: Handshake and versioning. Check: `initialize` returns protocol version and features; a major mismatch is refused; any other method before it is refused.

API-6.statement: One contract. Check: `schema.get` lists methods, event kinds and error codes; every response carries `seq_at`; the in-process adapter and the socket give identical results.

API-7.statement: State, units and runs. Check: state.get, units.list/get/history and runs.list equal the record files field for field.

API-8.statement: Usage, history, CI, versions. Check: values equal the records; unreadable or missing data is "unknown", never a guessed number.

API-9.statement: Health. Check: health.get gives each finding with a plain reason code and text.

B2-OUTCOME.statement:
**B2-OUTCOME — The project service records a finished child's outcome itself.**
A committed terminal whose orchestration is still open (active or paused), whose reservation is live, whose context is
`committed` and whose run belongs to the writer's own runtime and host class is recorded by the service on its own
writer, right after the result is safely stored and again by a bounded, fair sweep after a restart. The outcome is a
pure function of the store: the service's and the primary's records are byte-identical. One final predicate
(`ServiceRecordAuthority`, a required typed check) runs as the first statement of the admission transaction at the
service entry and at the primary's, so admission, close, interruption, the 24 h idle end and expiry meet at one
boundary; after any of those nothing new is recorded and "unrecorded" is final (owner decision 92.1 A). The primary's
later call on a recorded run is a read-only retrieval that writes nothing, works after a normal close, and never
changes who recorded it; its refusals are named and write nothing. Who recorded (`service` or `primary`) lives in a
small separate table keyed by the receipt id with no foreign key (schema step 19 -> 20, owner decision 92.3 A);
receipts, records and the enrolled operation set are unchanged; the service entry has no socket entry; the service
writes no QA and never sets `accepted`.
Source: DESIGN-0.4.0-B2-outcome.md draft 2 with the s2 corrections, rows B2-1 to B2-18; owner decision 92; docs/requirements/b2.md.

E1-1.statement: **E1-1 — Consent first.** RS-11, decision 90.11 A. Setup asks once, in plain words with the real reason, with a pick-list (yes / not now) and a details view, before the collector gets a login-start entry. Nothing is written or run without a yes; not now writes and runs nothing; a failed install is reported and not remembered. Tests: tests.test_login_start.OfferTests.test_E1_1_asks_once_with_reason_pick_list_and_details_and_installs_only_on_yes, tests.test_login_start.OfferTests.test_E1_1_a_failed_install_is_reported_and_not_remembered.

E1-10.statement: **E1-10 — The entry's command passes the runtime check.** The command the rendered entry holds (launchd ProgramArguments, systemd ExecStart), run as given, reaches require_authorized_collector_runtime and starts only when the state's authorized runtime is the installed one; with a different authorized digest it is refused with runtime_unauthorized. The CLI prints the refusal's message, not its code, so the run's printed refusal is matched to the message the collector's own check raises with that code. Tests: tests.test_login_start.CommandAuthorizationTests.test_E1_10_the_rendered_command_passes_require_authorized_collector_runtime, tests.test_login_start.CommandAuthorizationTests.test_E1_10_the_installed_command_run_as_given_is_refused_with_runtime_unauthorized (the rendered launchd command run as a real process against a temporary installed copy). The real launchd and systemd back-off on a real install stays an owner check.

E1-2.statement: **E1-2 — macOS entry.** A launchd user agent in the account's LaunchAgents folder runs the installed collector command (absolute paths, isolated Python, learning-serve) at login, restarts it after a crash with a throttle (KeepAlive on failure, ThrottleInterval), logs to the CoCoLo log folder, and holds no secret. Loaded through an injected runner (launchctl bootstrap), never the real one in tests. Test: tests.test_login_start.InstallTests.test_E1_2_launchd_plist_and_load.

E1-3.statement: **E1-3 — Linux entry.** A systemd user unit runs the same command, with Restart=on-failure, RestartSec and StartLimit back-off, logs to the CoCoLo log folder, WantedBy=default.target, and no secret; enabled through the injected runner (systemctl --user). Test: tests.test_login_start.InstallTests.test_E1_3_systemd_unit_and_enable.

E1-4.statement: **E1-4 — Ask once.** The answer (yes or no) is kept in the private installer folder beside the project list. A re-run of setup does not ask again; with no private place to keep the answer, setup does not ask and says so; an update never asks. Tests: tests.test_login_start.OfferTests.test_E1_4_answered_is_not_asked_again, tests.test_login_start.OfferTests.test_E1_4_no_place_to_keep_the_answer_means_no_question, tests.test_login_start.AnswerTests.test_E1_4_answer_round_trip_and_refusals.

E1-5.statement: **E1-5 — Removal.** Removing unloads the entry through the runner, deletes its file, records no, and works when the file is already gone or the unload fails. Offered under Configure when the entry is on. Tests: tests.test_login_start.RemoveTests.test_E1_5_remove_unloads_and_deletes, tests.test_login_start.RemoveTests.test_E1_5_remove_tolerates_missing_file_and_failed_unload, tests.test_login_start.OfferTests.test_E1_5_configure_offers_remove_when_on_and_turn_on_when_off.

E1-6.statement: **E1-6 — Refusals.** A relative command path, a symlinked entry path, an existing entry that is another user's or that others can change, or an unsupported system is refused with a plain reason and changes nothing; the entry is written through folder descriptors opened without following a link. Tests: tests.test_login_start.InstallTests.test_E1_6_refusals_change_nothing, tests.test_login_start.OfferTests.test_E1_6_unsupported_system_is_not_asked, tests.test_login_start.ReviewFixTests.test_E1_6_an_entry_another_user_owns_or_others_can_change_is_not_replaced.

E1-7.statement: **E1-7 — Wired into setup.** The collector step offers login start after the collector is ready, in setup (an update never asks), through the audited terminal runner; the existing Configure menu is unchanged. Test: tests.test_login_start.WiringTests.test_E1_7_setup_offers_login_start_after_the_collector_is_ready.

E1-8.statement: **E1-8 — Status reports the entry.** Setup's status lines report the login entry as on, off or stale. Stale means the entry's command no longer matches the installed collector's path, or the installed runtime's identity (the digest the owner authorized) is not the one the entry was last written for, or that identity cannot be read. The entry is read only through folder descriptors opened without following a link, never blocking on a FIFO or device, and only when it is the owner's and others cannot change it; otherwise it is stale. A status line holds no private value: no digest, key or folder path; its reason is one of a fixed set. Tests: tests.test_login_start.StatusTests.test_E1_8_status_is_on_off_or_stale_and_names_no_private_value, tests.test_login_start.StatusTests.test_E1_8_the_runtime_identity_is_read_only_from_a_private_plain_authorization_file, tests.test_login_start.ReviewFixTests.test_E1_8_status_never_follows_a_link_or_blocks_on_a_special_file_or_reads_another_users_entry.

E1-9.statement: **E1-9 — An update keeps the entry current.** When consent is already recorded (E1-4: an update never asks), an update that changes the collector's path or the authorized runtime digest rewrites the existing entry through the runner and records what it was written for; when it cannot, the entry is reported stale with a plain reason and the earlier entry is kept. The authorized runtime is the one the collector's own active-identity check (require_authorized_collector_runtime: exact schema, not quiesced, owner-only, never through a link) accepts for this setup's attested runtime; any other is reported stale and nothing is written. An update never asks and never creates an entry, whatever its answers file says. The record and the answer are read only from owner-only plain files of the owner's, never through a link or blocking. A failure shows a fixed reason with no path; when the record cannot be kept the earlier entry is put back and the entry is not shown as refreshed. An entry that is current is not rewritten; with no recorded yes, or with no entry, nothing is written. Tests: tests.test_login_start.ReviewFixTests.test_E1_9_a_rewrite_needs_the_collectors_active_identity_for_the_attested_runtime, tests.test_login_start.ReviewFixTests.test_E1_9_the_runtime_record_and_the_answer_are_read_only_from_private_plain_files_of_this_user, tests.test_login_start.ReviewFixTests.test_E1_9_an_update_never_creates_an_entry_from_an_answers_file, tests.test_login_start.ReviewFixTests.test_E1_9_a_failed_rewrite_shows_a_fixed_reason_with_no_path, tests.test_login_start.ReviewFixTests.test_E1_9_a_failed_record_write_keeps_the_earlier_entry_and_is_not_shown_as_refreshed, tests.test_login_start.UpgradeTests.test_E1_9_an_update_that_moves_the_collector_rewrites_the_entry_without_asking, tests.test_login_start.UpgradeTests.test_E1_9_an_update_that_changes_the_runtime_digest_rewrites_the_entry, tests.test_login_start.UpgradeTests.test_E1_9_an_entry_that_cannot_be_rewritten_is_reported_stale_with_a_reason, tests.test_login_start.UpgradeTests.test_E1_9_a_current_entry_a_missing_entry_and_no_consent_write_nothing.

LEGACY-H1B.statement:
**LEGACY-H1B — Listed refusal codes have a plain next step.**
Every code in the union of OPEN_REASON_CODES, DISPATCH_REASONS, START_REASONS, SERVICE_REFUSALS and
HISTORY_REASON_CODES resolves to a non-default next step that starts with an uppercase ASCII letter, contains no
forward or backward slash, is 11 to 241 characters long, and ends with a full stop or closing parenthesis.

LEGACY-HOLD-LIFECYCLE.statement:
**LEGACY-HOLD-LIFECYCLE — Existing hold lifecycle boundary checks.**
With real in-process account and project services, the baseline has zero live results, account slots and pending
bindings; opening a run increments pending bindings by one with limit 4096; account-hold status reports the binding
increment, exactly the run_slot, binding and probe kinds, and an Account holds summary naming binding. Recording a
completed run eventually leaves zero account slots and at most one live result. Settling a lost run writes exactly
one released slot with release kind lost. Cancelling a container run removes its container, eventually releases its
slot and leaves no failed stop. A container that cannot stop reports cancel_requested and an attention message,
keeps its slot across repeated stop attempts, then releases it after a retried stop succeeds.

LEGACY-HOLD-LIFECYCLE-B0-2.statement:
**LEGACY-HOLD-LIFECYCLE-B0-2 — Deferred run supervisor reservation settlement.**
A reservation left by a stopped service exists and eventually receives its lost terminal. B0-2 gates the run
supervisor and remains skipped under the owner's narrowed B0 scope of 2026-11-20. Its registered executable
obligation remains not_run and supplies no passing coverage until that deferred work is executed.

ML-R91.statement: **ML-R91 — Recorded empty folder trees.** Owner decision 91=A: a folder that holds only other empty folders CoCoLo itself made counts as empty, provided there is nothing else inside and every folder matches the device/inode identity CoCoLo recorded. Foreign files, unrecorded folders, and replaced folder identities do not qualify. The two C-3 checks must enforce this rule without accepting foreign contents.

RS-B-5.statement:
**RS-B-5 — Authenticated withdrawal of an unclaimed open.**
The project service and the opening host class may withdraw an unclaimed open with matching enrolled project,
caller scope, run id, inputs digest, attempt custody and current binding generation. Authentication precedes
immutable receipt replay; an exact replay remains available after the binding is pruned. Different callers receive
no receipt. New transitions refuse claimed, fenced, withdrawn or stale bindings; missing generations are refused.
Withdrawal evidence is retained for the tombstone's life. The project records its withdrawal duty before registration,
marks the complete request releasing before dropping memory, retries identical requests after lost replies, and
withdraws never-claimed cancellations, pre-preparation failures, idle registrations (one hour, owner decision 90.7)
and stopped-service registrations. A registration refusal preserves the duty; a faulted writer gets one memory
withdrawal, otherwise account expiry. Armed leases belong to the fence path.
Source: DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-B.md draft 3 §4, §7 and rows W1-W5 (W4a-e), M7; PLAN-0.4.0-supervisor-slices.md B3.

RS-D-2-N1.statement:
**RS-D-2-N1 — Eligible changed-runtime closure.**
After a runtime change, the real `end_earlier` sweep closes an eligible orchestration as
interrupted. Recorded results and verified account releases permit closure. The ordinary
expiry pass releases committed custody `orchestration_closed`. Count each update-ended
orchestration with any unrecorded result once as `ended_by_update_unrecorded`, including
after restart and result retirement/purge. Expose only a count, never result content.
Same-runtime and other-service sweeps do nothing. The close and its count commit atomically.

RS-D-2-N2.statement:
**RS-D-2-N2 — Unfinished changed-runtime custody.**
Without verified account release, an unrecorded result prevents close. Keep the orchestration
open and committed body/context custody charged until its retention deadline; at that deadline
release custody `retention`, without inventing release evidence or counting an update closure.
Corrupt release evidence cannot close it. No pre-commit deadline retires reserved custody (SH-4).

RS-D-D2.statement:
**RS-D-D2 — Deadlines and retention of result custody.**
No deadline before the commit retires a lease-born reservation: a reserved row past its lease deadline stays charged and
publishable while its RS-B obligation is held, and is retired only after RS-B releases that obligation (SH-4, RS-4);
a row that lacks its hold is kept and reported, never retired by a deadline. Committed custody is released `retention`
exactly at `retained_until_ms`, judged at max(wall, persisted floor), so a moved-back clock revives nothing and blocks no
pass (RS-D-7). A closed orchestration releases committed custody `orchestration_closed`, but an unattended close does not
end custody (owner decision 90.8). A verifier opens only when its worker outlasts the verifier's lease by one hour (owner
decision 90.4); a worker expiring while the verifier runs leaves the verifier's custody live, and a record on an expired
attempt is refused. A retiring row refuses body, context and admission reads. Only the lease path (`prepare_lease`) is
reachable from product code: the non-lease `prepare` is refused at runtime on any lane built without the local-reference allowance (the service runtime's lane).
Source: DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-D.md draft 2 s1, s8, s9, draft 3 s8, rows D1-D4, C1-C3, V1-V4; DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-BD-shared.md SH-3, SH-4; docs/requirements/d2.md.

RS-D-D3.statement:
**RS-D-D3 — Crash-safe retirement and the context sweep.**
Retirement records `retiring` (custody released, reads refused), unlinks the fixed names without opening or following them
(a missing, corrupt, wrong-mode, extra-hard-link, symlink, FIFO or link-pair entry is unlinked as an entry), fsyncs the
directory, and only then records `expired`; a stop at any step is finished by the next pass, and the charge is kept until
`expired`. Only a directory under a fixed name needs repair: the row stays `retiring` and charged, its context is
`repair_required` with the reason, it is shown by `result_retirement_repairs`, retried every pass, and other custody keeps
retiring in the same pass; an unlink or fsync error keeps the row `retiring`, charged and retried. The context sweep finishes
context-only custody (custody released, no reservation row, or its own `retiring` / `repair_required` retry) with no
reservation row read or written, and never selects a context that has a reservation. Start-up reconciliation removes orphan
and partial context and body files and one name of a link pair using directory listing and `lstat` only: no body or context
bytes are read, and its work does not grow with the number of tombstones (RS-D-9). A 1 MiB body is returned through every
chunk (K2).
Source: DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-D.md draft 3 s4-s6, draft 4 s1, rows U1-U10, K1, K2, S1; DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-BD-shared.md SH-3 (retirement); docs/requirements/d3.md.

RS-D-D4.statement:
**RS-D-D4 — Publication material and replay.**
The prepare transaction stores the exact prepared material (the canonical bytes whose keyed digest is `prepared_digest`) in
`project_result_publications`; the commit transaction removes it, and so does the transaction that records `retiring`. A
failed publication with the service live is retried from the kept packet (the live lane keeps it until its own commit) and
commits once, reusing the final body file, with `prepared_digest` and `retained_until_ms` unchanged. A publication is committed
from the store, by a successor or by settlement arbitration, only while it is still eligible, decided inside the commit
transaction: the reservation is `reserved`, its RS-B obligation row is `held`, the context is `bound`, and the stored material
verifies (its digest, binding, assignment digest, terminal record, usage record and the final body's digest); no deadline is a
condition. An ineligible or altered publication is refused (`history_conflict` when altered) and only finishes cleanup. Before
the account is asked to settle an attempt the project writer arbitrates it: `recovered` (a verifiable body is committed
first), `unrecoverable` (the obligation row goes `releasing`, so no publication of that attempt, live or replayed, commits
afterwards) or `settling` (a `releasing` row or a settlement row already exists: nothing is committed, cleanup follows). A
stop before the body's final link leaves a run that RS-B's settlement ends lost, with no half-recorded state; a result is
lost only when the service stops before a verifiable final body exists (RS-D-12 as narrowed; no numeric bound, owner
decision 90.1 A and 90.2 A). A replay that commits a claim that has a live job is adopted by the lane once.
Source: DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-D.md draft 3 s1-s3, s6, draft 4 s2-s4, rows P1, R1-R6, R3', R4', P2', P3', X1-X3, L1-L3; DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-BD-shared.md S-2, S-3; docs/requirements/d4.md.

RT-RX-1.statement:
### RT-RX-1 — One provider-state classifier

Routing snapshots, open admission, and the existing before-launch check shall derive usage state from the same classifier, with the same provider, account evidence and evaluation time. Its externally distinguishable states shall be `ample`, `constrained`, `exhausted`, and `unknown`. These are usage states, not admission verdicts or provider-configuration eligibility.

**Acceptance:** Identical evidence and time produce identical state in snapshot construction, open and launch; no second routing-only threshold, stale-reading rule, or optimistic state translation exists. An exhausted state produces `provider_exhausted` when earlier admission gates pass.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps open/launch's shared `headroom_state` use at `admission_metadata.py:284` and `admission_metadata.py:481`; changes the three-state/default-ample classifier at `admission_metadata.py:379` and the state-free route interface at `routing.py:1836`. Authority: 124.2; analysis lines 14–19.

RT-RX-10.statement:
### RT-RX-10 — Escalation remains meaningful after a usage switch

When the surviving selected setting is on the configured family ladder, keep existing failure qualification and escalation semantics: attempt 2 uses the next eligible higher rung when qualified, attempt 3 uses the strongest eligible higher rung, and no higher eligible rung retains the current surviving pick. Filter exhausted providers throughout. Do not silently disable an otherwise applicable escalation solely because the provider was switched for usage. A surviving setting absent from the ladder needs the explicit resolution in OPEN-4; no invented strength order is specified here.

**Acceptance:** A usage switch to an on-ladder setting still yields `next`, `strongest`, or `none_higher` according to the surviving ladder, with correct from/to settings. Unconfirmed judgment failures remain held and non-ladder families still do not escalate. A usage switch alone must not produce a misleading successful quality escalation or an unexplained `off_ladder`; the off-ladder fixture remains an explicit unresolved case until OPEN-4 is settled.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps failure qualification at `routing.py:1532`–`routing.py:1562` and rung semantics at `routing.py:1567`–`routing.py:1580`; addresses `off_ladder` at `routing.py:1563`. Authority: 124.3; analysis line 13.

RT-RX-11.statement:
### RT-RX-11 — Verifier selection keeps the other-provider preference

For a worker's actual selected provider, prefer the other eligible, non-exhausted provider, then the worker's own eligible, non-exhausted provider. Use the existing family/risk verifier model, effort and agent rules. Constrained/unknown state shall not demote a preferred verifier. Verification tasks for known work shall use this same rule with the actual worker provider and bound outcome, rather than reuse an obsolete advertised verifier blindly.

**Acceptance:** For both worker providers, every risk and supported family, a non-exhausted eligible other provider wins even if constrained/unknown. If it exhausts, the worker's provider is the fallback when eligible and non-exhausted. If neither is available, no verifier is invented. With unchanged state, advertised and actual verification routes agree on provider/model/effort; meaningful work still requires verification and verification does not recursively require verification.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps preference and risk settings at `routing.py:1473`/`routing.py:1489`, known-work selection at `routing.py:1608`, and verification requirement at `routing.py:1734`; extends `_select_verifier` at `routing.py:1458` with usage filtering. Authority: 124.1.

RT-RX-12.statement:
### RT-RX-12 — Same-provider verification is always non-independent

Whenever the verifier's actual provider equals its worker's actual provider, the advertised verifier and actual verification route shall explicitly record `independent=false`, regardless of family, risk, policy version or escalation scope. The marker shall survive a verifier re-pick. A different provider shall not acquire this false marker merely from a previous advertised fallback, and provider diversity alone shall not attest a completed independent verification verdict.

**Acceptance:** Cross-product assertions over both providers, all risks and all supported worker families find explicit false on every same-provider pair, including high/critical, default installations and families outside judgment scope. A re-pick from other-provider to same-provider becomes false. A re-pick back to a different provider does not retain false from the old route; execution/verdict audit remains unobserved until real evidence arrives.

**Keeps/changes:** Broadens conditional marking at `routing.py:1506`, scope checks at `routing.py:1618`/`routing.py:1744`, and actual-route projection at `routing.py:1822`; keeps route-versus-observation distinction at `routing.py:1810`. Authority: 124.4.

RT-RX-13.statement:
### RT-RX-13 — Re-pick the verifier at its own open

The worker route's verifier is a recommendation at that snapshot time. At the verifier's own open, obtain current trusted state and select the verifier again using the worker's actual provider, original verification family/risk, and bound worker outcome. If the advertised provider has become exhausted since the worker route, select the remaining eligible provider, apply RT-RX-12, and admit that actual verifier normally. Do not rerun, relabel or replace the completed worker to avoid this race.

**Acceptance:** A worker routed at t1 advertises the other provider; that provider exhausts before verification at t2. The verifier open chooses the eligible survivor with the correct verifier model/effort, records both recommendations and the reason for change, marks same-provider false, and keeps the same worker/outcome binding. If both exhaust at t2, verification is unsatisfied; a worker result alone is not recorded as verified.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps known-work route correspondence at `routing.py:1608`, risk selection at `routing.py:1617`, and final usage check at `admission_metadata.py:287`; changes reliance on the earlier advertisement at `routing.py:1737`. Authority: analysis line 12 and 124.1/124.4.

RT-RX-14.statement:
### RT-RX-14 — At most one exhaustion-triggered re-route at open

For each logical child open (worker or verifier), a fresh open denial whose reason is exactly `provider_exhausted` may cause one automatic refresh of the trusted snapshot, re-route, and alternative open. This is at most two open attempts total for that logical child, including across replay/recovery; it is not an unbounded provider ping-pong. The replacement still uses normal admission, account-wide run caps, task attempt limits and execution bounds. A second exhaustion denial terminates recovery with an explicit unsuccessful outcome; both exhausted uses RT-RX-16. Non-exhaustion denials do not trigger this mechanism.

**Acceptance:** A provider becoming exhausted between route and open causes zero launches there and at most one alternative open. Inject a second exhaustion denial: no third open occurs, including after a replay. A survivor at its cap returns `window_run_cap_reached` and is not launched or retried via another provider under this mechanism. Passing admissions are counted normally and never charged twice; denied opens do not create admitted runs. Keep logical task/parent/outcome lineage and link both attempts in audit. Durable retry ownership is OPEN-5.

**Keeps/changes:** Adds bounded recovery around `admission_metadata.py:287`; keeps account cap at `admission_metadata.py:289`, future-admission counting at `admission_metadata.py:296`, route bounds at `routing.py:1751`, and authoritative original-open evaluation at `account_open_admission.py:44`. Authority: analysis lines 14–15 and standing rule.

RT-RX-15.statement:
### RT-RX-15 — Admission and before-launch checks retain final authority

A non-exhausted route snapshot is advisory. Open shall still perform the full current admission sequence, and launch shall still perform its existing recheck. Preserve API-key refusal, identity/client/subscription checks, owner attestation, paid-usage/spend-control restrictions, billing freshness/bootstrap limits, run caps, signature/current-permission checks and atomic original-open behavior. Only the headroom classifier correction in 124.2 changes admission permission; reporting unknown separately does not deny an otherwise admitted unknown window.

**Acceptance:** A route selecting any provider cannot bypass each existing denial reason when independently injected. Exhaustion arriving after open still prevents launch. An unknown Codex window with valid remaining evidence still admits. API-key, paid usage, missing identity/attestation, billing and cap denials keep their existing priority and cannot be treated as exhaustion-triggered failover. Launch does not recount the admission cap.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps fixed-order gates at `admission_metadata.py:207`–`admission_metadata.py:307`, launch rules at `admission_metadata.py:431`–`admission_metadata.py:483`, and raw recapture/commit authority at `account_open_admission.py:3`; changes only RT-RX-1–5's headroom semantics. Authority: standing rule.

RT-RX-16.statement:
### RT-RX-16 — Structured result when both providers are exhausted

When both provider states are exhausted, return a structured, non-executable unsatisfied routing result instead of `ContractError`, for worker selection and verifier selection, including refresh/re-route paths. Its observable contract shall contain an unsatisfied discriminator, cause `provider_exhausted`, task identity, selection phase (worker/verifier), snapshot evaluation time/reference, and entries keyed by both `codex` and `claude`, each with state `exhausted`, account scope, deciding evidence/reason and next known reset or explicit null. Do not fill successful execution fields with a fake selected worker/verifier. Exact wire names/version are OPEN-6; these semantic fields are required.

**Acceptance:** Both exhausted yields an inspectable result naming both providers and their states, never either no-candidate exception. Known future reset times are surfaced; absent reset stays null, with fallback expiry separate. With multiple blocking explicit windows, the next known reset is the earliest future reset among the applicable blocking windows, not a guarantee that all restrictions end then; later blockers remain inspectable. Consumers stop without launch or a success/verified claim. A successful worker whose verifier is unsatisfied retains its worker result and an unsatisfied verification phase.

**Keeps/changes:** Changes usage-caused no-candidate behavior at `routing.py:1683` and `routing.py:1510`; extends successful-only output at `routing.py:1773`. Authority: 124.5; resolves the missing shape noted at analysis line 9 at the semantic level.

RT-RX-17.statement:
### RT-RX-17 — Bridge/configuration failure is a separate cause

Usage routing shall not turn on `codex_primary_may_bridge_to_claude` or bypass disabled providers, model allowlists, unavailable agents or bridged-write containment. With Codex exhausted and Claude not exhausted but blocked by the Codex-primary bridge flag, report the distinct bridge/configuration no-candidate cause, not “both exhausted.” Preserve existing policy-only `ContractError` behavior for invalid inputs and no eligible configured candidates; 124.5 does not authorize converting every error to exhaustion. If both states really are exhausted, RT-RX-16 applies and any additional policy exclusions remain separately visible.

**Acceptance:** With both providers enabled, bridge=false, Codex-primary and Codex exhausted/Claude ample, no Claude launch occurs and the diagnostic identifies the bridge prohibition separately from Codex exhaustion. Turning the flag on makes an otherwise eligible Claude candidate selectable. Disabling both providers with no exhausted evidence retains existing no-candidate refusal. Invalid primary/task/configuration still fails closed. Exact mixed-cause diagnostic representation is OPEN-6.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps bridge flag at `routing.py:1287`, provider/model allowlists at `routing.py:1271`, writable mapping exclusion at `routing.py:1666`, and policy-only no-candidate errors at `routing.py:1684`; adds distinct usage-versus-policy diagnostics. Authority: 124.1; analysis lines 12–13.

RT-RX-18.statement:
### RT-RX-18 — Availability audit coexists with v5 selection identity

Record a separately identifiable provider-availability audit alongside the existing selection audit: classifier/snapshot format identity, evaluation time and snapshot reference, per-provider account/state/evidence/reset/fallback expiry, candidates considered in policy order and their skip causes, actual worker/verifier choice, usage-driven switch, and re-route count/trigger with original and replacement open references. Preserve policy/configuration/mapping digests and existing risk/escalation/failure lineage. For unopted v6 cells, keep `selection.policy_version=5` and the existing selection identity; do not relabel those cells v6 or conflate availability with policy/model selection.

**Acceptance:** Audit reconstructs why a worker/verifier skipped each provider and distinguishes `unknown` from `ample`, usage from bridge exclusion, quality escalation from usage switch, and initial route from open recovery. For an unaffected unopted cell, the legacy selection subtree is identical and its policy version remains 5; added availability data lives outside that subtree. Requested settings remain distinct from observed execution and verdicts. Same-provider marking required by 124.4 is still present even when it changes the full route serialization.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps explicit v5 identity at `routing.py:1754`–`routing.py:1760`, provider config digest at `routing.py:1792`, mapping digest at `routing.py:1824`, and observed/verdict placeholders at `routing.py:1809`–`routing.py:1815`; adds availability audit outside `_selection_metadata` use at `routing.py:1753`. Authority: analysis line 10, 124.2/124.4/124.5.

RT-RX-19.statement:
### RT-RX-19 — Evidence remains attributable and bounded

The snapshot/audit shall reference trusted identity and deciding headroom/billing evidence, plus the later clearing reading when it supersedes resetless evidence. Evidence from another project may decide account state, but shall retain its owning-project provenance; do not falsely present foreign references as locally held admission evidence. Preserve bounded admission evidence and existing project-local citation filtering. A Codex billing-only exhaustion must have an attributable billing reason/reference even if no headroom digest exists. Do not expose raw account identifiers or authentication secrets.

**Acceptance:** Cross-project exhaustion and clearing are reproducible using resolvable, scoped snapshot evidence, while stored admission citations remain a subset of that project's held records. A large history does not produce an unbounded list of admission digests. Billing-only exhaustion is explainable without a fabricated headroom reference; unknown does not cite imaginary favorable evidence. Raw provider credentials/identity values do not appear in routing audit. Snapshot size limits are OPEN-3.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps evidence intersection at `admission_metadata.py:200`, bounded deciding-level intent at `admission_metadata.py:388`, and local citation construction at `account_open_admission.py:29`; addresses billing-only state without a headroom digest at `admission_metadata.py:413`–`admission_metadata.py:418`. Authority: standing admission rule and analysis lines 11/14.

RT-RX-2.statement:
### RT-RX-2 — State boundaries and unknown evidence

A live numeric window at or above 90% exhausts either provider; 75% through below 90% is constrained; usable live numeric readings below 75% are ample in the absence of a stronger applicable restriction. Claude `rejected` exhausts and `allowed_warning` constrains even for an empty windows collection, subject to RT-RX-3–5. The most restrictive applicable evidence wins except for the expressly authorized supersession. Missing Codex windows, all-null utilization, or only expired usage evidence shall be reported as unknown when no other applicable evidence establishes a state. Unknown shall not be invented as ample, shall not cause a usage skip, and shall pass the headroom gate at open; other admission gates still apply. Keep the current Codex `ordinary_usage_allowed=false` exhaustion rule separately identifiable as a billing-derived usage restriction.

**Acceptance:** Both providers classify numeric 74.99/75/89.99/90 as ample/constrained/constrained/exhausted; either a second live 90% window or Claude rejection dominates a low numeric reading. A Codex account with no usable window is `known: false` ("unknown") in the route snapshot, remains a routing candidate, is still rated ample by admission's headroom_state, and is admitted with otherwise passing evidence. Codex ordinary-usage denial remains exhausted, including the existing future-evidence case. Partial numeric coverage and Claude allowed-without-utilization are OPEN-2.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps thresholds/status precedence at `admission_metadata.py:29`, `admission_metadata.py:64`, and billing exhaustion at `admission_metadata.py:407`. KEEPS admission's three-value rating vocabulary (exhausted/constrained/ample) and its ample default for absent or expired evidence (`admission_metadata.py:88`, `:395`) unchanged (primary 2026-11-24: no new stored or returned rating value; shrinking/expanding validated vocabularies breaks real-ledger upgrades). "Unknown" exists only in the route's provider-state snapshot, as `known: false` for a provider with no applicable evidence, and in the route audit. Authority: 124.1 and standing rule.

RT-RX-20.statement:
### RT-RX-20 — Collection, compaction and replays preserve the classifier's answer

Evidence retention/merge/capture must preserve enough trusted later favorable evidence to implement 124.2; a collector that drops every favorable reading after a rejection cannot satisfy it. Compaction, cross-project capture, overflow, restart or replay shall neither resurrect a superseded resetless restriction nor drop an explicit live/future-stamped restriction. Preserve billing restrictions and cap accounting independently. No requirement here authorizes a new arbitrary observation append or weakens evidence authenticity.

**Acceptance:** The same sequence of resetless restrictive then later non-restrictive readings yields the same state before and after overflow/merge/capture/restart; explicit unreset and rollback cases stay restrictive through the same operations. Replay does not duplicate run admissions or restart the RT-RX-14 retry allowance. Existing bounded histories still work. Retention changes must be limited to evidence needed for the new classifier; the exact storage design remains implementation work.

**Keeps/changes:** Extends the account-wide evidence contract at `admission_metadata.py:178` and `account_open_admission.py:24`; changes the old unconditional restrictive-wins assumption at `admission_metadata.py:170`. Existing retention behavior is exposed by `test_providers.py:1398` and `test_providers.py:2608`; those behaviors cannot silently defeat 124.2. Authority: 124.2 and standing rule.

RT-RX-21.statement:
### RT-RX-21 — Preserve named regression behavior, with explicit authorized exceptions

The regression inventory below shall remain the preservation baseline. Tests whose assertions conflict directly with 124.2/124.4 or additive availability audit must be identified for narrow future revision, not cited as evidence that the owner decision can be ignored. This step does not edit tests, fixtures or golden files.

**Acceptance:** A later implementation's validation report names these existing tests, preserves unaffected assertions, and accounts explicitly for each changed assertion under RT-RX-1–20. No blanket golden regeneration hides unrelated provider/model/effort/risk/bounds/lineage changes. Existing no-candidate configuration errors remain covered separately from new both-exhausted results.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps the behaviors exercised at the file:line locations below; permits only the exceptions stated below. Especially preserve `routing.py:1603` and `routing.py:1759`, while applying 124.2/124.4 to their affected outputs.

RT-RX-3.statement:
### RT-RX-3 — A later non-restrictive reading clears a resetless restriction

For the same provider and account, a restrictive headroom reading with no reset time, including an empty-window Claude rejection/warning or a restrictive window with `resets_at=null`, shall cease contributing its restriction when superseded by a later trusted non-restrictive reading. Do not require that reading to originate in the same project, run, or probe. This exception shall not clear an independent explicit unreset window or billing/paid-usage restriction. Mixed readings must retain any explicit unreset restrictive component.

**Acceptance:** A resetless 95% reading at t1 followed by a trusted 10% reading at t2, with t1 < t2 <= evaluation time, no longer exhausts; an empty-window Claude rejection followed by a later allowed 10% reading similarly clears. A reading for another account/provider or an older favorable reading does not clear. A separate explicit live 95% window still exhausts. Assert identical outcomes at route, open, and launch. Chronology ties and the complete meaning of non-restrictive are OPEN-1/2.

**Keeps/changes:** Changes unconditional restrictive-wins at `admission_metadata.py:170` and `admission_metadata.py:397`; keeps provider/account filtering at `admission_metadata.py:400`. Authority: 124.2; analysis lines 16–19.

RT-RX-4.statement:
### RT-RX-4 — Resetless headroom lasts five hours, not a day

Without a superseding reading, a resetless restrictive headroom reading shall expire after five hours from its observation time, including an empty-window status-only reading. Keep the existing inclusive age-bound convention: it still restricts at exactly five hours and expires at five hours plus one millisecond. The 24-hour horizon for paid usage and spend control shall remain unchanged. Do not manufacture a provider reset timestamp from this fallback expiry.

**Acceptance:** At ages five hours minus one millisecond, five hours, and five hours plus one millisecond, a resetless rejection/95% reading is restrictive, restrictive, then no longer restrictive. With no usable remaining reading the usage state is unknown, not ample. Paid-usage and spend-control evidence six hours old still denies under their existing rules. Audit distinguishes fallback expiry from a measured reset.

**Keeps/changes:** Changes resetless lifetime at `admission_metadata.py:55` and `admission_metadata.py:75`; keeps five-hour constant at `admission_metadata.py:38`, age comparison convention at `admission_metadata.py:61`, and billing horizons at `admission_metadata.py:328` and `admission_metadata.py:349`. Authority: 124.2.

RT-RX-5.statement:
### RT-RX-5 — Explicit resets and rollback protection

An explicit restrictive window with `resets_at > evaluation_time` shall remain restrictive despite a later favorable reading, until that reset. At the reset it no longer contributes. An expired explicit window shall not acquire a fresh resetless lifetime. A future-stamped restrictive observation shall not disappear merely because the evaluation clock moved backward; an older favorable reading cannot clear it.

**Acceptance:** At reset minus one millisecond an explicit 95% window still exhausts despite a later 10% reading; at reset it does not. The same assertions apply to an explicit Claude rejected window. A future resetless rejection/95% reading survives rollback even with an older ample record present; an explicitly elapsed window stays elapsed even if its observation is future-stamped. Future favorable supersession is OPEN-1.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps `admission_metadata.py:57`, `admission_metadata.py:59`, and `admission_metadata.py:398`; narrows restrictive-wins only as RT-RX-3 permits. Authority: 124.2.

RT-RX-6.statement:
### RT-RX-6 — Account selection and account-wide evidence

The trusted snapshot builder shall supply the route's account scope separately for Codex and Claude. It shall learn each account fingerprint from the trusted provider identity selected by the same freshness and latest-reading rules as open, not from task JSON, the primary-provider name, or a caller-selected account. Usage/billing evidence shall be filtered by that provider and fingerprint across projects, as at open. Missing identity shall remain distinguishable from a known account with unknown usage and shall not become admission permission.

**Acceptance:** Exhaustion for account A does not exhaust account B; exhaustion for A in another project does affect A. Switching the trusted current identity from A to B changes the snapshot's scope and records its identity evidence. An arbitrary task fingerprint cannot select B or clear A. Missing/stale identity still fails open's identity gate; a valid identity with no usage passes only the usage gate. Account changes between snapshot and open require current admission, never reuse of A's state as B's.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps identity selection at `admission_metadata.py:213`, account filtering at `admission_metadata.py:400`/`admission_metadata.py:410`, and account-wide inputs at `account_open_admission.py:19`/`account_open_admission.py:24`; changes the account-free route interface at `routing.py:1583`. Authority: standing rule; analysis line 11.

RT-RX-7.statement:
### RT-RX-7 — Trusted route input with time and evidence

Live routing shall receive a trusted provider-state snapshot built with RT-RX-1, separate from task data and from the existing task-shape `trusted_routing_evidence_refs`. The snapshot shall identify its evaluation time, project/context binding, each provider and selected account fingerprint (or explicitly unavailable identity), identity evidence, usage state, deciding evidence references, reasons, known reset information and fallback expiry where applicable. Equal inputs and evaluation time shall produce deterministic results. A supplied state label alone is not trusted evidence. Snapshot transport, validation limits and freshness policy are OPEN-3.

**Acceptance:** A live route's recorded states and references match the builder's classification at the recorded time. Injecting an exhausted/ample label, fingerprint or evidence reference through task JSON cannot alter availability. A snapshot from another context cannot be treated as the current trusted snapshot. The snapshot grants no launch/admission authority. Offline behavior must explicitly distinguish unavailable live state; it must not claim ample (OPEN-3).

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps metadata's authority limitation at `admission_metadata.py:3` and trusted original-open boundary at `account_open_admission.py:3`; extends `routing.py:1587`/`routing.py:1836` and state-free callers such as `cli.py:1283`/`cli.py:2085`. RT-RX-8.statement:
### RT-RX-8 — Worker selection preserves policy order

Within the existing eligible provider/model/agent candidates, select the first policy-ordered candidate whose provider is not exhausted. Do not rank ample ahead of constrained or unknown, insert an unconfigured provider, change risk cells, or change model/effort merely because utilization differs below 90%. Usage skips are additional to existing configuration, allowlist, mapping and containment exclusions. The standing rule to continue on the other provider applies when that provider has an eligible candidate.

**Acceptance:** For each policy order and both primary providers, the first eligible candidate wins with ample/constrained/unknown states in any combination. At 90% the exhausted first provider is skipped and the next eligible provider wins with its existing model/effort/agent/dispatch. At 89.99% it is not skipped. Disabled, disallowed or unavailable-agent alternatives are never synthesized to continue work.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps first-eligible order at `routing.py:1603`, candidate construction at `routing.py:1639`, and configuration/agent exclusions at `routing.py:1660`; adds exhaustion filtering inside eligibility at `routing.py:1652`. Authority: 124.1 and standing rule; corrects the analysis's rejected reordering proposal at analysis line 9.

RT-RX-9.statement:
### RT-RX-9 — Exhaustion outranks every escalation or fallback choice

Every retry/escalation candidate shall pass the same exhaustion filter as the first worker pick. No ladder step, risk floor, legacy model fallback, or retry may restore an exhausted provider. A usage-driven provider switch shall not itself create a failed attempt, a semantic failure, evidence of independent verification, or entitlement to an additional attempt.

**Acceptance:** With the preferred/strongest ladder provider exhausted, attempts 1–3 never select it; an eligible surviving provider can continue even where the unavailable preferred setting was stronger. A usage switch leaves task failure count and failure evidence unchanged. If every provider is exhausted, return RT-RX-16 rather than forcing a ladder choice. Existing legacy-fallback authorization remains necessary and cannot bypass usage exclusion.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps escalation's `first_eligible` use at `routing.py:1573` and fallback authorization contract at `routing.py:1853`; extends eligibility at `routing.py:1652` and fallback configuration check at `routing.py:1711`. Authority: 124.3.

RT-RX-LIVE-ROOT-1.statement:
### RT-RX-LIVE-ROOT-1 — Installed CLI reads the account snapshot from the default state root

On an installed CLI (its install manifest present), a route command given the default `--state-root`, or none, reads the advisory provider-state snapshot from `default_state_root()`: `_require_own_roots` turns the checked default into None, and None there means the default, never "no state root". With the account service answering, availability is `checked`.

**Acceptance:** On the installed layout with real account and project services, `learning-route --state-root <default>`, `learning-route` without it, and `route` (which has no `--state-root` option) all return availability `checked` with the service's per-provider states and no `reason_code`.

**Keeps/changes:** Changes the `state_root is not None` gates at `cli.py` `_store_free_route` (snapshot and routing-evidence reads), the `route` command and `_validated_assignment_route`. Found live on the installed 0.8.54 (route not_checked with no reason, 2026-11-24); the source-tree tests have no install manifest and never took this path.

RT-RX-LIVE-ROOT-2.statement:
### RT-RX-LIVE-ROOT-2 — A not_checked route always says why

A route whose availability ends `not_checked` always carries `reason_code` `snapshot_unavailable:<reason>`, on every route call site, including when no state root resolves at all: the source tree run without `--state-root` (`snapshot_unavailable:no_state_root`; the developer's own default state is never read implicitly there) and an installed CLI whose default state root cannot be resolved.

**Acceptance:** Source tree without `--state-root`: `learning-route` and `route` return `not_checked` with `snapshot_unavailable:no_state_root`. Installed with a refused XDG_STATE_HOME: both return `not_checked` with a `snapshot_unavailable:` reason. No route returns `not_checked` without `reason_code`.

**Keeps/changes:** Extends RT-RX-7/RT-RX-18 (98f18967 gave reasons only where a state root was given). Keeps decision 3 (no service, no snapshot, selection unchanged); the reason is advisory and never changes a refusal or an admission.

RT-RX-LIVE-ROOT-3.statement:
### RT-RX-LIVE-ROOT-3 — The installed trust pin on the state root is unchanged

An installed CLI still refuses a non-default `--state-root` for its primary-host commands (`OwnRootRefused`), before any route or service work; the RT-RX-LIVE-ROOT-1 fix resolves only the default and gives a caller no way to move the state root.

**Acceptance:** On the installed layout, `learning-route --state-root <another folder>` exits 2 with the fixed refusal `--state-root is refused: an installed CLI uses only the default learning state`, and nothing is written in that folder.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps `_require_own_roots` (`cli.py`) as it is, including `args.state_root = None` for the accepted default, which LearningState/CollectorPaths and the legacy-state move read as the default.

TF-1.statement:
**TF-1 — Retain the supported runner and isolation.** Keep unittest and `scripts/parallel_tests.py`, the three
suites, module/stage/shard selection, separate worker processes and per-worker temporary directories, secret
stripping, and bounded worker teardown. A full normal run uses the runner's DEFAULT job count (no fixed 6).
Sharding/module splitting must not omit or duplicate tests. Preserve existing `load_tests` discovery hooks.
Witness: discovery and execution of inherited, ordinary, `load_tests`-filtered and generated unittest cases;
stable shard partition; failing worker and import error both make the
runner nonzero; child environments omit fixture secrets; concurrent workers have distinct temporary roots
and cannot see each other's fixture files; an intentionally stuck worker and its owned descendants are
reaped within the configured teardown bound with diagnostics; default jobs remains `max(1, (os.cpu_count() or 2) - 2)`.

TF-10.statement:
**TF-10 — Refuse real processes and git in unit/component.** Extend the existing audit guard, installed before
test-module imports, to both restricted layers. Deny subprocess starts, spawn, exec, fork/forkpty and system
shell calls; a real git invocation is denied regardless of executable spelling or wrapper. Fakes/in-process
functions remain allowed. Guard violations name layer, module, operation and test ID if known, and cannot be
turned into green by catching the exception (worker records the violation and fails at completion). Witness:
try each available process API, git under an absolute path, an import-time spawn and a caught denial; verify
no child-side marker is created. Run platform-specific API witnesses on their supported OS; the matrix must
contain evidence for both macOS and Linux.

Decision 100 A (2026-11-23): discovery and test workers, locally and in CI, inherit only an explicit environment allowlist: PATH, HOME, temporary-directory variables, locale variables, COCOLO_TEST_* and named framework necessities. Every other variable is dropped, including GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN and arbitrary *_PASSWORD variables. TF-10 witnesses must verify the actual worker boundary and permitted-variable controls.

TF-11.statement:
**TF-11 — Refuse real sockets in unit/component.** Deny socket creation/connect/bind and applicable address
resolution/network APIs before OS effects; include AF_UNIX and AF_INET and socketpair. Patch/audit supported
stdlib entry points without blocking construction of test doubles. Explicitly refuse socket.socket,
socket.socketpair, socket.create_connection, socket.create_server, socket.fromfd and socket.fromshare
(where available), connect/connect_ex/bind/listen/accept/sendto/sendmsg, and getaddrinfo/gethostbyname/
gethostbyname_ex/gethostbyaddr/getnameinfo. Cover asyncio open_connection/start_server and Unix variants
through the same underlying guards; there is no asyncio exemption without an explicit evidence-backed
requirement change. Existing creation/connect/bind/socketpair protections remain mandatory. The denial is sticky as in TF-10. Witness:
import-time creation, bind/connect, socketpair and caught denial fail without creating socket files or contacting
a service; in-memory transport fakes pass. Allowed-layer probes use only local fixture sockets.

TF-12.statement:
**TF-12 — Keep unit time deterministic.** Preserve the existing unit sleep prohibition; reject positive-duration
explicit waits/polls in unit tests (thread condition/event waits, select/poll and joins that would block).
Allow immediately ready/nonblocking operations and injected clocks. Component may wait on in-process
threads, subject to its budget. Witness: unit sleep still fails; a positive wait fails without waiting; zero-time
poll and a ready event succeed; a fake clock advances without real time. This is an accidental-I/O guard,
not a security sandbox against malicious tests using native libraries or disabling the harness.

TF-14.statement:
**TF-14 — One shared golden-output comparison.** Provide one stdlib test-only helper (about 30 lines of core
comparison/update logic; security/metadata checks may be separate). New/migrated file-based expected output
goes through it. The framework rejects new/migrated golden comparisons that bypass this helper;
a direct golden read-and-assert bypass must fail preflight. Ordinary scalar assertions stay allowed.
Exact bytes or canonical UTF-8 text comparison produces a bounded useful diff; missing
goldens fail. Deterministic, explicitly reviewed normalization happens before the helper; never silently mask
states, reason codes, content, permissions or evidence required by a statement. Ordinary scalar/value assertions
are not forced into snapshots. Witness: equal, differing and missing golden, binary or documented text-only
behavior, and a changed required reason code. Existing assertions are retained until a named equal proof exists.

TF-15.statement:
**TF-15 — Golden updates need explicit intent and requirement provenance.** A golden can be created or changed
only with exactly `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` AND a valid requirement ID supplied to the helper and declared by the
calling test. Fail closed for missing/unknown/unrelated IDs and other environment values. Restrict writes to
the checked-in test golden root; reject traversal and symlink escapes. Persist/review the requirement ID with
the golden change in an adjacent `<golden-name>.requirement` UTF-8 sidecar inside the checked-in golden
root, included in review with the golden; report update mode visibly, and do not count an update run as passing evidence. Witness:
unset/0/true without exact 1 cannot write; invalid ID and escape leave files untouched; authorized update
records its ID, and a subsequent normal run is needed for green evidence. Never update a golden to fit code
that contradicts its requirement.

TF-16.statement:
**TF-16 — Only pinned test-only dependencies.** Hypothesis is the only newly introduced third-party test tool.
Record its exact version and SHA-256 artifact hash(es) in a test-only requirements file; also pin/hash required
transitive dependencies so a hash-required offline-prepared environment is reproducible. No shipped module,
runtime manifest, installer or provider imports/installs them. Keep shipped code stdlib only and runnable with
Python 3.11. Only the subsequently owner-authorized temporary test-only environment may receive these dependencies. Witness: static distribution-boundary check and a
shipped-code smoke test with test packages unavailable; dependency file rejects unpinned/unhashed additions.
Select/verify the concrete Hypothesis release and artifact hashes from primary sources in step 2, not from the
unverified version claim in a review packet. If an existing prepared interpreter lacks it, record that limitation
and use the authorized temporary test environment; do not silently skip required property checks.

TF-17.statement:
**TF-17 — Explicit reproducible Hypothesis profiles.** Provide test-only `dev` (20 examples), `ci` (100 examples,
`derandomize=True`), and `soak` (at least 1000 examples). Runs default to ci; dev and soak need explicit selection. Unknown profiles fail. I/O/stateful rules use `deadline=None`, and still obey module budgets and
hard timeouts. Keep unittest-compatible generated TestCases. Witness: inspect each loaded setting; reproduce
a deliberately failing state machine and verify its minimized trace and unittest failure are retained in the
runner log and yield nonzero. Parser compatibility must be demonstrated, not assumed from unittest ancestry.

TF-18.statement:
**TF-18 — Normal sampling and soak separation.** Normal crash runs include an in-memory disk model
with separate volatile and durable file-content, mode and namespace states. Writes change volatile file
contents; create/unlink/rename/exchange/mkdir/rmdir change volatile namespace links. A file flush persists
that file's complete bytes/mode; a directory flush persists that directory's name-to-object links, never
implicitly an unflushed child's contents. SQLite commit state is tracked separately. Crash discards volatile
state and exposes only durable contents reachable through durable namespace links; recovery is then checked
against the single ML invariant and table. Permitted outcomes include complete S or T according to the
durable row, preserved owner objects and named unrecorded directories; torn published contents, lost
owner edits and a history direction inconsistent with recovered contents are rejected.
Witnesses distinguish flushed from unflushed writes, creates and renames, including flushing only one
rename parent; a missing production flush must change the model's post-crash outcome and fail the check.
A checked-in `tests/merge-persistence-samples.json` names the normal sample inventory by operation,
phase, before/after side and commit label where applicable, plus stable occurrence/reproducer. Validate it
against discovered persistence-significant calls; every operation kind and relevant boundary needs a normal
sample. Normal selection includes the model and ci-profile generated cases, excluding complete sweeps.
Complete crash/fault sweeps, including recovery faults, run only under explicit `--profile soak` in
local-routing; soak includes the complete inventory, not merely persistence samples. Reject explicit soak
module selection with dev/ci, a complete-sweep request without soak, conflicting profile selectors and
unknown profiles. Report the effective profile and sample seed or minimized reproducer. The Linux/podman
power-loss lane is later work (81 A); kills and the model do not prove it, and this task installs no podman.

TF-19.statement:
**TF-19 — Preserve the single merge oracle and its review gate.** Step 3's `check_end_state` is derived from
sections 1, 2, 3 and 5 of `ANALYSIS-0.4.0-merge-library-states.md`, with one POLICY dictionary at Q1–Q6 recommended
defaults. Read durable history independently; never infer direction from a report or all-new tree. The state
machine selects land/retry/cancel/undo/crash/recover and fault points, not a second handwritten outcome oracle.
Trace every replaced assertion to a table cell and replacement file:line; primary checks the table line by line.
Witness: every permitted outcome in all 41 cells is ACCEPTED and deliberately wrong outcomes for each cell are rejected; the four required mutations (private-location
check, flush before A, third history commit, injected EIO falsely landed) each have a named catching test.
If a current test contradicts its requirement, stop on it and record test name, exact requirement and conflict;
the already-identified oracle corrections are requirement-driven work, not permission to fit expectations to code.

TF-2.statement:
**TF-2 — Every module declares one valid layer.** Before running bodies, reject missing, duplicate, unknown,
or stale module declarations and incompatible stage/layer pairs. Stale means no longer discovered. Check all discovered suites, including
modules selected out of the current run, and import failures; never silently default an undeclared module to
integration. Witness: remove one module's layer, add a bogus layer, add a stale entry, duplicate a JSON key,
or declare layer component with stage unit; each is rejected with the full module ID. Valid mappings above pass.

TF-20.statement:
**TF-20 — Scenario coverage uses the shared fixture and exact statements.** Step 4 extends the existing
`scripts/e2e_lifecycle.py` with a shared temporary project, prepared git repo, scripted stand-in Claude/Codex
binaries and service on a Unix socket. Build the shared project/providers first, then implement the
checks in six parts covering all 80 requirements. Cover all 80 requirements, not necessarily exactly 80 checks, in six
parts: API (27), G1–G9 (9), L12 (7), TERM (5), and two parts containing the other L requirements (32 total).
Parts do not multiply a module's budget; fragments aggregate under TF-8. Each part obeys the scenario budget, preserves all-flow checks and AND aggregation, and emits per-requirement
pass/fail with content-free reports. Every assertion matches its statement's exact reason codes/states. One
deliberate fault per group must make that group's checks red; shared G checks may also detect it and must
never be suppressed to obtain an 'exactly one group' presentation. `test_e2e_requirements` must pass unchanged
in meaning. Witness: all-80 execution, isolated and combined part execution, fault matrix, private-value checks.

TF-21.statement:
**TF-21 — Prune only with equivalent named proof.** After step 4, address the ten heaviest modules by
baseline job-seconds (`MEASURE-test-framework.md` top-ten rows, originally lines 92–101) before wider
pruning. Before each step-5 module change, record its requirement
IDs and keep/move/remove disposition. A removed test requires a named start-to-finish check proving the same
statement and relevant edge cases; a moved function test keeps identical assertions/expected values and cites
the requirement. Every removed/changed assertion is listed with old and replacement file:line; no weakening.
Keep real boundary checks per TF-13 and remeasure the affected module after each change, quoting the timing
file's job-seconds. Witness: report links to executed replacement and retained assertions, with before/after
measurements; metadata-only replacement is insufficient. No pruning precedes the matching scenario proof.

TF-22.statement:
**TF-22 — Review checkpoints and evidence.** Step reports are under 15 lines each and name commits,
requirements -> red/green or measurement evidence, every assertion replacement, and open issues. Owner subsequently set the next review stop after step 3 (step-1 review r1). Apply that stop before proceeding to steps 4–5. Use only own worktrees/branches; never push, install outside the authorized temporary test environment, or modify the
control project or 0.3.3. Step 2 is authorized; step 3 rebases the existing merge
branch only after step 2 is committed. Acceptance includes macOS and Linux / Python 3.11 evidence or an
explicit outstanding platform gate; this Mac run alone cannot prove portability.

TF-27.statement:

TF-3.statement:
**TF-3 — Requirement tags remain available and validated.** Use the stdlib test-only
`@requirements(...)` decorator at method or class level and lifecycle `@check(...)` tags.
Validate declared IDs and reciprocal catalogue links. Inheritance follows the actual method;
an override without a tag has no requirement claim. Untagged tests may run; CODEOWNERS and
assertion-diff make their edits reviewable without a frozen grandfather list.

TF-4.statement:
**TF-4 — Validate the requirement catalogue and report missing coverage.** Maintain unique
IDs, exact source statements, and valid reciprocal check links. Empty statements, bad source
links, unknown IDs, duplicate checks and dangling links fail metadata validation. Requirements
with no check are `unchecked`: report their count and IDs in run records and the runner's last
line. They do not fail a run. Catalogue membership alone never claims passing coverage.
Registered planned checks remain declarations, not evidence that a test ran.

TF-5.statement:
**TF-5 — Coverage metadata is not a passing outcome.** Requirements without checks are reported as unchecked and do not fail a run. A full gate reports a requirement passing only when
every registered required check has run and passed. A requirement whose only results are passes and skips is reported as `skipped` (not proved here) and does not fail the run (decision 126.2: a skip is environmental, e.g. no disk image or socket). Missing, errored, assertion-free lifecycle checks,
and unexpected successes cannot establish a passing requirement. Partial runs report unselected requirements
as not run, never green; global structural validation still runs, and the selected checks determine runtime
results. Expected failures also cannot count as a passing proof. Preserve `Phase.expect` assertion counting and requirement-level AND across all scenario parts,
including G1–G9 checks selected for every affected flow. Witness: two checks for one ID, one failing or
missing from a shard result, cannot aggregate to pass; skipped-only proofs report `skipped` and expected-failure-only proofs fail;
neither is coverage. An assertion-free lifecycle proof and an unexpected success both fail the coverage gate. Assertion counting
is not proof of semantic correctness: review against the statement and fault sensitivity are also required.

TF-6.statement:
**TF-6 — Make duplicate slow proof reviewable.** Every non-unit new or migrated test declares a nonempty
`why_not_scenario` rationale (class-level rationale may cover inherited cases) naming the boundary, fault,
concurrency or edge condition a named lifecycle check cannot prove, or records that it IS the canonical
scenario check. Enforce presence; review truth against the requirement. Witness: a tagged non-unit test (including a fast one) without
the rationale fails and names its ID. Untagged tests do not claim requirement coverage and need no rationale metadata.
Rationale alone never authorizes deleting another proof.

TF-7.statement:
**TF-7 — Test edit review.** Retired (decision 126, test reset A).
Replacement: ordinary PR review with `.github/CODEOWNERS` covering tests and framework/CI
sources, plus the stdlib `scripts/assertion_diff.py BASE HEAD` report of added, removed and
changed assertions and deleted test methods. No legacy source/dependency/value fingerprints,
shrink-only lists, migration approval or trusted-base gate remain. `--base` is accepted for CI
compatibility and has no validation effect.

TF-8.statement:
**TF-8 — Enforce complete module budgets.** Sum actual worker-fragment job-seconds per
module, report every offender, and preserve complete/disjoint shard validation. Keep the
current non-ceiling budget-debt files and their warnings, regression limits and complete-run
retirement signal. New modules receive their layer budget. Historical Git replay, immutable
budget-ceiling files and trusted-base comparisons are retired (decision 126, test reset A);
replacement: current measured totals, ordinary review of debt changes, and CI run artifacts.

TF-9.statement:
**TF-9 — Preserve honest timing and timeout evidence.** Save per-worker elapsed values and run identity,
selected tests, actual jobs, platform/interpreter, completion/timeout status and module totals. Sum only
current-run workers for job-seconds (never stale seed timings, module totals plus per-test estimates, or CPU).
Keep wall time separate; report discovery and preflight seconds separately from worker job-seconds,
including on preflight failure. Always write available measurements on test failure and timeout. Name timed-out
workers and keep their diagnostic log. The scheduler's historical estimates are not measurements. Witness:
seed timings with obsolete entries, fail one worker and time out another; current totals and diagnostics remain
correct. Hard worker timeout is a safety bound separate from the module's budget. Overall elapsed time is
reported without a five-minute failure threshold.
